text:
alex: rolled out continuous-batcher heuristic v1.7 to prod at 03:20 UTC — seeing p99 for short requests jump ~3x and aggregate throughput down ~18% on g4s-prod. anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

perf-bot: alert: batcher.p99_latency spike detected at 2056123450; throughput -18% vs baseline (1h).

maria: looking into it. did we change the token_budget target or the queue-window in that rollout? i remember a tweak to small_batch_merge_threshold in the PR.

devon: i rolled the merge_threshold revert on a single pool (pool-7) and p99 returned to baseline there. can reproduce on canary too.

alex: noted rollback. can someone paste a quick profiler snippet? i'm seeing a lot more kernel fallbacks to the slow path in traces.

maria: attaching a short tracer snip from the affected host: 

```text
[2056123451] batch_form: (requests=78) avg_seq_len 14 -> formed_batches 36
[2056123451] batch_shapes: variance 0.72, dominant_shape [1,16] count 18
[2056123451] chosen_kernel: fallback_fp16_slow_path (count 312)
[2056123451] kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.62 -> 0.33
[2056123451] token_budget: target 256 -> actual_alloc 96 (floor breach)
```

jin: interesting — token budget collapsed on many requests. looks like the heuristic aggressively shrank per-request budgets to reduce tail for some large workloads, but that caused more heterogeneous batches and triggered conservative kernel selection.

devon: my local repro: when batch_shape variance > 0.6, the kernel selector chooses slower, general kernel 2.7x more frequently. hypothesis: merge_threshold change increased small-request merging which increased shape variance under mixed traffic.

maria: agreed. propose temporary mitigation: bump token_budget floor to 128 and disable shape-based preemption for the first 50ms of batch formation. also revert the merge_threshold tweak in main.

alex: can we A/B this on canary? devon, can you spin up cb-v1.7b with those mitigations?

devon: done — canary cb-v1.7b running with token_floor=128 + preemption_hold=50ms. early numbers: p95 improved ~12%, overall throughput still -6% but p99 down from 3x -> 1.4x. kernel_switches: 89 -> 32 on canary; kv hit rate recovers to ~0.58.

maria: promising. long-term fix: update batch_shape scoring to prefer homogeneous-by-kernel groups (score = shape_sim * kv_confidence) before applying token budget reductions.

alex: schedule a controlled rollback/patch window. call SRE for rollout coordination and perf regression job. @jin please add a short synthetic that targets the <32-token path to validate.

jin: added a quick generator and snippet to stress test short-paths: 

```bash
# synthetic short requests at ~100rps
while true; do curl -s -X POST $REDWOOD_URL/generate -d '{"input":"ok","max_tokens":16}' & sleep 0.01; done
```

perf-bot: benchmark job queued: job/continuous-batcher-abtest-2056123500 (canary vs baseline).

devon: saving traces/logs to /mnt/perf/2056123456-batcher-debug.log for the postmortem.

alex: plan summary: 1) revert merge_threshold tweak 2) land token_budget floor 128 + preemption_hold 50ms 3) update kernel routing weights next sprint. rolling tomorrow 02:00 UTC with canary first. :thumbsup:

maria: i'll open the follow-up PR and include the microbench results. will post the changelist here once ready.

alex: thanks everyone — keep updates in this thread after the patch lands.
